context.prd-excerpt:
Project: Link Shelf (slug link-shelf). Project type: greenfield. Project path: C:/Users/Lee/AppData/Local/Temp/oq7-qn0r6zml/poor/app
The PRD's tech stack: Python 3.11, FastAPI 0.110+, SQLAlchemy 2.x, SQLite (file-backed, no server process), pytest 8.x. Backend only - no frontend, no container runtime.
The PRD declares three dependencies: fastapi, sqlalchemy, pytest. A fourth, httpx, is added here and is NOT a product decision: FastAPI 0.110+ ships starlette's TestClient, which requires httpx at runtime, and every endpoint task's verification runs pytest against that TestClient. Without httpx declared, L3-002's smoke test and every later endpoint test fail at import with an error about a missing optional dependency rather than about the code under test.
SQLite is deliberate: "SQLite rather than PostgreSQL so the whole project runs with no external service: a fixture that needs a database server running is a fixture that fails for reasons unrelated to what is being tested." SQLite ships with CPython, so it needs no entry in the dependency list.
No migration tool. Neither the declared stack nor the dependency list contains Alembic or any alternative. L4-001 creates the schema with Base.metadata.create_all. Do NOT add alembic, do NOT add a migrations directory, and do NOT add a versioned migration chain -- that would introduce an undeclared dependency.
pytest configuration lives in this same file, under [tool.pytest.ini_options]. That is why there is no pytest.ini, no setup.cfg and no tox.ini: keeping the configuration here means pytest setup costs zero extra files.

task.objective: Write pyproject.toml declaring the project metadata, the four runtime dependencies (fastapi, sqlalchemy, pytest, httpx), the explicit setuptools package list, and the pytest configuration -- all in one file.

requirements.requirement:
Create file `pyproject.toml` at the repository root with exactly the content between the two markers below.
The `<![CDATA[` and `]]>` markers are XML packaging so that the version bounds survive intact in this task file. They are NOT part of pyproject.toml -- do not copy either marker into the file.
[build-system] requires = ["setuptools>=68"] build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"
[project] name = "link-shelf" version = "0.1.0" description = "Save a link, list saved links newest first, and tag them." requires-python = ">=3.11" dependencies = [ "fastapi>=0.110", "sqlalchemy>=2.0,<3", "pytest>=8,<9", "httpx", ]
[tool.setuptools] packages = ["app", "app.api", "app.models", "app.schemas"]
[tool.pytest.ini_options] testpaths = ["tests"]

The `[tool.setuptools] packages` list MUST be written out explicitly as shown, and must NOT be replaced with a `find` directive or deleted in favour of automatic discovery.
Reason: it pins what the distribution installs to this file. Without it, setuptools falls back to flat-layout auto-discovery, which decides what ships by applying its own built-in exclude list -- and that built-in list is the only thing keeping the root-level `tests` package out of the distribution.
Be clear about the strength of this claim: auto-discovery does produce the correct result for this tree on current setuptools. This is therefore a determinism choice, not a workaround for a build failure. Naming the four packages makes the installed set a property of pyproject.toml rather than of whichever setuptools version happens to be installed.
Consequence for later layers: every module layers 3 and 4 add lands inside `app`, `app.api`, `app.models` or `app.schemas`, all four of which are listed, so no later task needs to touch this list. A task that introduced a NEW subpackage of `app` would have to add it here, because a package that is not listed is silently omitted from a non-editable build.

pytest, though a test-only tool, goes in `[project].dependencies` rather than in an optional-dependencies group. L0-004 installs with a plain `pip install -e .` and then runs pytest; putting pytest in an extra would mean that command installs no test runner and L0-004's own verification could not run.

`httpx` is declared with no version bound. The PRD pins fastapi, sqlalchemy and pytest; httpx is a transitive requirement of starlette's TestClient and is pinned by whatever fastapi resolves to. Adding a bound here that fastapi disagrees with would produce a resolver conflict at install time for no benefit.

Do NOT create pytest.ini, setup.cfg, setup.py, tox.ini, requirements.txt or requirements-dev.txt. All configuration belongs in pyproject.toml.
Do NOT create a virtual environment and do NOT run pip. L0-004 does both.
Do NOT modify .gitignore, app/__init__.py or tests/__init__.py.

test-requirements.test: Verify the file exists and is valid TOML: `python -c "import tomllib,pathlib; tomllib.loads(pathlib.Path('pyproject.toml').read_text(encoding='utf-8')); print('valid toml')"` Expected: exit code 0, stdout contains `valid toml`.

Verify project name and Python floor: `python -c "import tomllib,pathlib,sys; d=tomllib.loads(pathlib.Path('pyproject.toml').read_text(encoding='utf-8')); p=d['project']; print(p['name'], p['requires-python']); sys.exit(0 if p['name']=='link-shelf' and p['requires-python']=='>=3.11' else 1)"` Expected: exit code 0, stdout shows `link-shelf >=3.11`.

Verify all four dependencies are declared, by distribution name. The regex matches the leading name and stops at the first character that cannot appear in one, which is how the version bound is discarded without writing it out: `python -c "import tomllib,pathlib,re,sys; d=tomllib.loads(pathlib.Path('pyproject.toml').read_text(encoding='utf-8')); names={re.match(r'[A-Za-z0-9._-]+', s).group(0).lower() for s in d['project']['dependencies']}; want={'fastapi','sqlalchemy','pytest','httpx'}; print('missing:', sorted(want-names)); sys.exit(0 if want.issubset(names) else 1)"` Expected: exit code 0, stdout shows `missing: []`.

Verify the declared version bounds match the PRD's stack. Each expected bound is rebuilt from character codes so this test file never has to contain a raw less-than sign; chr(60) is `<` and chr(62) is `>`: `python -c "import tomllib,pathlib,sys; d=tomllib.loads(pathlib.Path('pyproject.toml').read_text(encoding='utf-8')); deps=set(d['project']['dependencies']); ge=chr(62)+'='; lt=chr(60); want={'fastapi'+ge+'0.110', 'sqlalchemy'+ge+'2.0,'+lt+'3', 'pytest'+ge+'8,'+lt+'9'}; print('missing:', sorted(want-deps)); sys.exit(0 if want.issubset(deps) else 1)"` Expected: exit code 0, stdout shows `missing: []`.

Verify the explicit setuptools package list is present and complete, so the installed package set is pinned by this file as requirement 2 describes: `python -c "import tomllib,pathlib,sys; d=tomllib.loads(pathlib.Path('pyproject.toml').read_text(encoding='utf-8')); got=d['tool']['setuptools']['packages']; print(got); sys.exit(0 if sorted(got)==['app','app.api','app.models','app.schemas'] else 1)"` Expected: exit code 0, stdout lists the four packages.

Verify pytest configuration lives in this file and points at tests/: `python -c "import tomllib,pathlib,sys; d=tomllib.loads(pathlib.Path('pyproject.toml').read_text(encoding='utf-8')); tp=d['tool']['pytest']['ini_options']['testpaths']; print(tp); sys.exit(0 if tp==['tests'] else 1)"` Expected: exit code 0, stdout shows `['tests']`.

Verify no migration tool was introduced: `python -c "import pathlib,sys; t=pathlib.Path('pyproject.toml').read_text(encoding='utf-8').lower(); sys.exit(1 if 'alembic' in t else 0)"` Expected: exit code 0 (alembic must NOT appear; schema creation is Base.metadata.create_all in L4-001).

Verify no competing configuration file was created: `python -c "import pathlib,sys; bad=[n for n in ('pytest.ini','setup.cfg','setup.py','tox.ini','requirements.txt') if pathlib.Path(n).exists()]; print('unexpected:', bad); sys.exit(0 if not bad else 1)"` Expected: exit code 0, stdout shows `unexpected: []`.

Verify no XML packaging marker leaked from requirement 1 into the written file: `python -c "import pathlib,sys; t=pathlib.Path('pyproject.toml').read_text(encoding='utf-8'); sys.exit(1 if 'CDATA' in t or ']]' in t else 0)"` Expected: exit code 0.
